item.title: Russia begins 3 days of voting in a parliamentary election set to cement the Kremlin's power
item.description:
Russian State Duma elections began Friday — the first since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Voting is also taking place in the areas annexed from Ukraine in the east as Putin looks to reinforce popular support for the war. OSCE election observers are not invited to monitor the outcome of the elections, a telling signal, critics say, that the Kremlin has no intentions of conducting free and fair elections. "Russia’s refusal to invite an election observation mission seriously breaches its international commitments and shows a worrying disregard for democratic standards. Election observation is not optional — it is something that all OSCE participating States have agreed to, and it is a cornerstone of transparency and accountability," OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President Pere Joan Pons told Fox News Digital. item.title: What Trump’s attacks on mail-in voting mean for the midterms
item.description:
The extraordinary danger is that a president who believes he is the law, and the law is him, remains intent on disrupting the electoral process This was originally published in The Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox For the millions of Americans who vote by mail – almost a third of the country – the week began with significant uncertainty that they would be able to easily submit their ballot this fall, thanks to a March executive order from Donald Trump that aimed to restrict mail-in ballots. By Monday night, the supreme court restored a measure of order by rebuking the president and rejecting his plan – but Trump’s frothing response portends more danger for the rapidly approaching midterms. item.title: Climate change made deadly Nepal glacier and rock collapse more likely, analysis finds
item.description:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning. Continue reading...

item.title: The cost of Iran’s regional leverage
item.description:
Yemen's Houthi armed forces patrol the capital Sanaa on Sept. 12, 2026. Mohammed Huwaish/AFP via Getty Images It took just a few days for Houthi forces to seize most of Yemen’s Red Sea coast , including the shores of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait , a crucial Red Sea maritime choke point. The offensive started on Sept. 3, 2026, with a push to cut the strategically important road linking the city of Taiz to the port of Mokha. By Sept. 11, Mokha, the town of Dhubab and the island of Mayyun, in the mouth of the strait, were under Houthi control . The Yemeni rebel group seized some 2,100 square miles of territory , forcing more than 100,000 people to flee, according to the U.N., with many making the risky journey to nearby Djibouti by boats. item.description:

Most Western companies quickly sold their Russian operations and holdings after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the Kremlin has since made it difficult for firms to leave the country.

item.title: Alex Ovechkin claims he’s ‘not in politics’. His pro-Putin video says the opposite
item.description:
After the NHL star appeared in an ad campaign for United Russia, it’s fair to start pressing about the impact of his stances – even if he doesn’t want to talk about it When Russian launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, reporters asked Washington Capitals captain Alexander Ovechkin for his thoughts. It was no secret, even then, that Ovechkin was close to Vladimir Putin. Years before, Ovechkin boosted the Russian president in a social media campaign and featured Putin in his own Instagram profile photo. “He is my president,” Ovechkin said of Putin shortly after the invasion. “But [like] I said, I’m not in politics, I’m an athlete.” That’s over. He’s in politics now. “The thing about the video: I’m Russian,” Ovechkin told reporters Thursday. item.title: Pete Hegseth is rebuilding the Army’s ‘brass ceiling’
item.description:
Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump attend a dignified transfer on July 22, 2026, for casualties of the Iran war. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images News via Getty Images Dan Driscoll resigned as secretary of the Army on Aug. 31, 2026. His departure leaves the Army without a Senate-confirmed civilian leader six months into the war with Iran, its busiest period since the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. Driscoll’s resignation was reportedly motivated, at least in part, by his frustration with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth . Earlier in August, Hegseth had blocked the promotions of four Army officers. Since his appointment in January 2025, Hegseth has fired or blocked the promotions of more than 80 admirals and generals . item.title: Poorest countries hit hardest by UK aid cuts under Keir Starmer government, new figures reveal
item.description:
As the executive director of the Living Independent Network Corp, Jeremy Maxand does what he can to help people who don’t drive get around in southern Idaho. As in most of rural America, public transit options are limited. The nonprofit organization, which serves those with disabilities, receives $100,000 annually from the state through a federal appropriation. The money finances cards riders use to pay for transportation, but Maxand described the region’s transit as a “bare-minimum lifeline service” and “piecemeal.” And yet, even that could soon worsen. The surface transportation programs authorized by the $1.2 trillion Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act , signed by President Joe Biden in 2021, expire by the end of the year.
